author: American Catholic Tribune
title: St. Rose of Lima begins construction on new parish center in Poinciana
text:
St. Rose of Lima begins construction on new parish center in Poinciana
St. Rose of Lima Parish held a groundbreaking ceremony for its new parish center on the Kissimmee campus, presided over by Bishop John Noonan on Aug. 16.
The planned 8,300-square-foot building will accommodate more than 500 people and feature a full commercial kitchen, allowing the parish to host social gatherings and expand ministry efforts for those in need in the Poinciana area. Bishop Noonan reflected during his bilingual homily on the journey to find suitable property and complete ongoing construction projects during his tenure as bishop of Orlando. “The struggle was where to build, because we decided that (the first location) was not the best, and it took a few years to… come to this place where we are now.”
He said, “You good people of Rose of Lima, wanted this church so much that you sacrificed to give for this building.” The original church groundbreaking occurred almost exactly ten years earlier, on Aug. 13, 2016.
Bishop Noonan drew a parallel between parishioners’ persistence and that of the Canaanite woman from Matthew 15: “She persists, just like you, the people of Rose of Lima, persisted that you wanted to have the church here. You too have been strong in your belief that you wanted this community of St. Rose of Lima,” he said. “You have built this church, and now you want to have a place where you can share and build up the faith community, through the faith of our young people, by sharing (and) teaching them who Jesus Christ is.”
After Mass concluded with a blessing at the site alongside clergy and benefactors from St. Rose of Lima as well as key partners from the construction team. With construction set to begin next week, Bishop Noonan mentioned plans for further expansion after completion: once finished with the parish center project, St. Rose aims to expand its church facilities.
“You have put your roots into this soil,” said Bishop Noonan. “You have allowed yourself to grow in your love, your faith for God… your home is here forever.” The Diocese of Orlando was established in 1968 and includes Brevard, Lake, Marion, Orange, Osceola, Polk, Seminole, Sumter and Volusia Counties; it comprises 79 parishes along with missions and Catholic schools under Bishop James Noonan’s leadership, according to the Diocese of Orlando.
